title: The Frozen Counter
subtitle: An interval that never sees the new state.
description: A setInterval started in an effect reads state that never updates.
options: It never renders any number because setState inside setInterval is illegal
It reaches 1 and sticks there: the callback closed over count = 0 forever, so every tick sets 0 + 1
It counts twice as fast because the effect re-runs on every render
It counts correctly; the empty dependency array is fine here
hints: Which value of `count` did the interval callback capture, and when?
What does the setCount(c => c + 1) form receive as its argument?

solution.summary: The correct answer is B — It reaches 1 and sticks there: the callback closed over count = 0 forever, so every tick sets 0 + 1
solution.answer: It reaches 1 and sticks there: the callback closed over count = 0 forever, so every tick sets 0 + 1
reasoning: Effects capture the render’s values; with [], the capture is from the first render only.
The functional update setCount(c => c + 1) reads the LATEST state and fixes this without re-subscribing.
Alternatively, listing [count] re-creates the interval each tick — correct but churny.
whyNot: It never renders any number because setState inside setInterval is illegal — setState is perfectly legal from timers — the problem is the stale value.
It counts twice as fast because the effect re-runs on every render — The effect runs exactly once because of the empty dependency array.
It counts correctly; the empty dependency array is fine here — The empty array IS the bug paired with reading state from the closure.
